newsitem.title: USA: Marijuana seizures way up along Texas border.
newsitem.headline: Marijuana seizures way up along Texas border.

text.p: Marijuana seizures along the U.S.-Mexican border have soared in recent days, indicating that Latin American growers are having a bumper year, officials said on Thursday.

Since Columbus Day, Oct. 12, which is a traditional high point of the marijuana smuggling year, the U.S. Border Patrol and the U.S. Customs Service in Texas and New Mexico have seized marijuana worth millions of dollars, as well as large amounts of cocaine and heroin.
Border Patrol spokesman Doug Mosier said seizures are up 50 percent over the same key period last year.
"The marijuana harvesting season appears to be in full swing," he said.
Mosier said September and October are big months in the Latin American marijuana harvesting season although growers in many countries, including Mexico and Colombia, grow the plants all year round.
Twenty people from Mexico, Texas, New Mexico, California and New York were arrested in separate busts on Columbus Day alone.
"It's been extremely busy since Columbus Day. Perhaps the smuggling community thought the U.S. Customs Service would relax," said Gurdit Dhillon, Customs management centre director.
So far this year, federal agencies report seizing about $500 million in drugs in El Paso and southern New Mexico. That is up about 44 percent from last year.
